statement: Tuning candidates should be chosen by the comparison's strictly proper primary loss (squared error, log loss or ranked probability score) pooled over every inner validation row (sum of w*loss / sum of w, survey-weighted under the population answer), not by an average of per-fold scores such as R-squared, and never by AUC or accuracy.
claimed_basis: RECIPES §4.2 'Score' row; MODELING_SEQUENCE ruling 4 (strictly proper primary); RECIPES F5 (RidgeCV averaged per-fold R-squared); §7.3 'tuning on AUC or accuracy' impossible by construction.
notes: [part id F1-010] choose() at tuning.py:1016. test_tuning_plan.py::test_the_pooled_loss_is_the_weighted_mean_of_every_inner_rows_loss checks the arithmetic only. [Merged F1-011 at turbotab/core/models/pipeline.py:532; its basis: RECIPES §4.2 'Score'; tuning.Loss restricted to validation.PER_ROW_LOSSES' strictly proper primaries (tuning.py:88).; its notes: Which outcomes trigger it depends on metrics.PRIMARY (another fork's file).]

statement: When a unit's rows repeat, feature-wise intervals that treat rows as independent would be too narrow, so the tests use CR2 with Bell-McCaffrey degrees of freedom, and above 200 exposures (CR2 computed per exposure) the intervals are refused rather than reported as independent.
regime: inference; feature-wise family; clustered rows; more than 200 exposures for the refusal
user_sees: "`pid` repeats, and cluster-robust intervals for 5,000 separate tests are beyond what TurboTab computes (200 at most); intervals that treated the rows as independent would be too narrow, so none is reported."
claimed_basis: none stated beyond the sentence (CR2 / Bell–McCaffrey from the math layer, inference.cr2).
notes: [part id F3-018] 200 is a compute limit, not a methods threshold. The exit is to combine each unit's rows into one.

statement: The regression-calibration interval is the percentile interval of the bootstrap resamples, 200 by default, and is shown only when at least 90% of the resamples could be calibrated; resamples whose day-to-day error swamped the between-person spread are dropped, which may pull the interval's end away from zero too near.
decision: interval reported or withheld for the calibrated coefficient
user_sees: "The interval is the percentile interval of {n} bootstrap resamples." / "{k} of {n} bootstrap resamples could be calibrated (...); fewer than 90% of them, so no interval is shown."
claimed_basis: MIN_BOOT_SHARE labeled 'a stated floor'; no source for 200 percentile resamples.
notes: [part id F5-033] Contradicts the app's own rule elsewhere that a percentile interval needs 1,000 to 2,000 refits (decisions.py:448-451 MAX_BOOT comment citing Carpenter & Bithell 2000; methods/substitution.py PERCENTILE_MIN_REFITS=1000; stages/modeling.py:43). The ms5 coverage simulation used 100 resamples and passed, which partly supports adequacy in that setting; the 90% floor is a convention.

statement: When the exposure family holds exactly one exposure-role column, the choice of multiplicity method changes no p-value or interval, so the stated multiplicity default moves from the Confirm sweep to For the record.
regime: Estimate or Describe; exactly one column with role exposure
decision: Whether the set_multiplicity default is a Confirm line or For the record
user_sees: For the record: "The family holds one study factor, so there is no other test to account for."
claimed_basis: none stated (the family is every exposure-role column, EstimandSpec.family)
notes: [part id F6-017] A single exposure can still yield several tests (quintile contrasts, spline terms, a declared modifier's interaction tests; sweep.py:473-477 says a withdrawn modifier is 'kept only to count its test'). Referee should check whether the app's multiplicity method ever acts on those; if it does, the line is silenced wrongly. Similar silencing at sweep.py:168-181: no candidate modifier column means the modification default changes nothing (a logic claim).

statement: The specification curve must not be fitted or shown before the analysis plan is locked: seeing specification estimates first would invite choosing the plan by its estimate (Gelman & Loken's forking paths).
regime: Estimate an effect; recorded choices with declared alternatives
decision: specification curve (Which of my decisions mattered?), after the lock
user_sees: "The specification curve opens after Fit locks the plan: shown before, it would invite choosing the plan by its estimate."
claimed_basis: calm/FOUNDATION §5 rule 6; Gelman & Loken 2013; BLUEPRINT §11 (after the lock)

statement: When some group of trial participants all had the event or none did (logistic separation), the model's risks run to 0% or 100% and no finite estimate exists, so the standardized risk difference and ratio are refused.
user_sees: Some group of people here all had the event, or none did, so the model's risk for them runs to 0% or 100% and no finite estimate exists.
notes: _logistic trials.py:715-743 also refuses when |β| > 25 or any fitted risk < 1e-10; GEE at 1135-1136. The marginal (standardized) risks remain finite under separation (fitted risks of 0 or 1 average to a finite risk); only the coefficients diverge, so 'no finite estimate exists' is overstated for the risk difference.

statement: For a numeric exposure, a cross-fitted R² of 0.9 or more of the exposure on the covariates (a variance inflation factor of 10) is a practical positivity violation: the effect rests on little of the exposure's own variation and extrapolates where it does not vary, so the estimate is refused until every row is kept on the record.
regime: inference; numeric exposure; DML-PLR or PDS
user_sees: The covariates explain 93% of `x`'s variance (at least 90%, a variance inflation factor of 10 or more): the effect rests on little of the variation of what you study itself, and the estimate extrapol…
claimed_basis: Kutner, Nachtsheim & Neter 2004 §10.5 (VIF 10, 'the conventional line'); the app's convention
notes: VIF 10 is a collinearity rule of thumb, not a positivity criterion: a global R² does not show whether the exposure varies at every covariate level. The record is the only exit (no trimming for a numeric exposure). Also stages/causal.py:512-518, 584-588, 736-748.

statement: A reliability estimated from internal consistency (α or ω) omits transient (occasion-specific) error, so a correction based on it under-corrects, whereas a test-retest repeat administration includes transient error.
decision: label on corrections from internal consistency; ranking of test-retest above ω
user_sees: "A reliability from internal consistency omits transient error, so the correction under-corrects (Schmidt, Le & Ilies 2003)."
claimed_basis: Schmidt, Le & Ilies 2003 (Psychol Methods 8:206); MODELING_SEQUENCE §0 ruling 8
notes: Also methods/scales.py:111-114 and the methods sentence core/scales.py:1008-1010. Ranking effect: rc_test_retest 'recommended', rc_internal_consistency 'available' (core/scales.py:128-145), so it is partly tier 1.

statement: When a repeating identifier's cluster reading is unsettled, not grouping by it ('no clustering without a confirmed unit') is the conservative path: the held-out draw and the folds group only by a settled cluster reading, and an identifier that rode along unconfirmed groups nothing.
regime: Any table with a repeating column read as an identifier but not confirmed; the seal (held-out split) and resampling folds.
decision: Whether the held-out split and folds keep a unit's rows together.
user_sees: No grouping of the held-out draw by the unconfirmed column; the seal basis notes its repeating contradicts 'one row per unit' (seal.py).
claimed_basis: readings.py module docstring lists it among the 'conservative path[s]'; BLUEPRINT §14.1 / §14 rule 2 (seal.py:209 comment).
notes: Likely mislabelled: for held-out and CV scores, splitting a unit's rows across train and test is the anti-conservative (optimistic) direction; asking (as inference does) is the conservative one. Implemented in turbotab/core/stages/rows.py:1951 (split_inputs) and turbotab/core/seal.py:209-219 (decide_basis 'unconfirmed ... never groups the draw, but its repeating still contradicts one row per unit'). Referee should check what decide_basis then shows. Overlaps the seal/rows inventory. | Inventory source id: F3-004.

statement: The injection order and the analytical batch along which QC-RLSC fits each feature's drift cannot be settled from the values (a sample number is also all-distinct; a preparation plate or a study group run in blocks also forms contiguous blocks); the guesses are a column named as a run order holding complete distinct numbers, else a whole-number permutation of the row positions, and batch columns named batch/run/plate (2+ levels, each on more than one row, at most n/4 levels), else a column whose levels each occupy one unbroken stretch of the injection order; at most two batch candidates are offered beside 'one curve over the whole run', and the user's choice settles them.
regime: Metabolomics/assay data offered QC-RLSC drift correction.
decision: Columns QC-RLSC uses for drift order and batch.
user_sees: QC-RLSC options, each naming its order and batch column (or 'one curve over the whole run').
claimed_basis: MS7 repair; METABOLOMICS_PACK §01 (name-blind reading); KIND_RULES injection_order/batch readings.py:1308, :1330.
notes: injection_order_reading readings.py:3139; MAX_BATCH_CANDIDATES :3124. Overlaps the qc_drift inventory. | Inventory source id: F3-037.

statement: Under inference, QRILC is refused for values below detection because it fills each value with a single draw outside the multiple imputation, so the intervals would not carry the imputation uncertainty.
user_sees: Refusal qrilc_under_inference: "QRILC fills each value below detection once, outside the multiple imputation, so the intervals would not carry that uncertainty."
claimed_basis: None cited beyond the reasoning; contract rung 'refused' (omics.py:1895).
notes: Behavior pinned by test_ms7_omics::test_4c. Note the same logic would apply to half-minimum (a single deterministic value) which is allowed under inference at <=10% and with attestation above. | Inventory source id: F5-013.

statement: When a unit's rows are repeated measurements of one quantity, averaging k of them cuts within-person variance k-fold.
regime: repeated rows answered 'repeats' (e.g., 24-hour recalls); aggregation by mean; k = the median rows per unit
notes: test_coach.py:143 checks the text only. True only for the error variance of a person's mean, and only if replicate errors are independent with equal variance; content.py:557-561 says consecutive-day recalls have correlated errors, so the cut is smaller. 'Within-person variance' itself does not change; k is the median count, not each unit's.

statement: In metabolomics data, missing values that cluster in the lowest-abundance features are likely below detection and not missing at random.
decision: the left-censoring finding's route to the non-detection fill
user_sees: Missing values cluster in the lowest-abundance features: likely below detection, not missing at random.
notes: Low-abundance missingness can also come from peak-picking or alignment failures (MAR/MCAR); the detector's threshold lives in the pack.

statement: Rows that are imputed copies of one record (e.g., NHANES DXA's five imputations) are, under inference, each analyzed as a completed dataset and the estimates pooled by Rubin's rules, which carries the imputation's uncertainty.
regime: inference; rows read as imputed copies
user_sees: each copy is analyzed as a completed dataset with its own outcome and the estimates pooled by Rubin's rules, which carries the imputation's uncertainty (NCHS's combining rules)
notes: Contradicts the teaching option (content.py:541-543: 'under inference kept only as a recorded limitation'). Rubin's rules carry the imputation uncertainty properly only if the provider's imputation was proper and congenial with the analysis.

statement: Results wording starts at the design's floor, an association for an observational design; causal wording is offered only for trials, 'an estimated effect, its assumptions named' only when no standing question points elsewhere and no stated assumption is refuted, and model explanations are never worded as effects.
decision: the drafted wordings and the noticing on stronger user wording
user_sees: "Between groups of people observed as they were: an association, not what would happen if anyone changed their diet."
notes: BEATS_MODELS_RESULTS.md:501, 683; content.py:404-411. It is in tension with the causal lane (DML/TMLE), which offers effect estimates in observational data under declared assumptions.
